header.running_head: Gatherings of Knowledge and Being in the Company of Ulema

blocks.text: asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Which of our companions are best?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "The person who reminds you of Allaah when you look at him, whose speech increases your knowledge and whose deeds remind you of the Aakhirah." [^1]
Hadhrat Qurra (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sat in a gathering, the Sahabah (RA) would sit in groups around him (to learn and teach, asking Rasulullaah ﷺ when they needed to)." [^2]
The Gatherings of the Sahabah (RA) after the Fajr Salaah

Hadhrat Yazeed Raqaashi says that after narrating Ahadeeth to them, Hadhrat Anas (RA) would say, "By Allaah! This Hadith has not been learnt as you people learn when people gather around a person who lectures to them. What used to happen is that the Sahabah (RA) used to sit in groups after the Fajr salaah to recite the Qur'aan and learn the compulsory and optional aspects of Deen." [^3]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Sits with a Gathering of the Sahabah (RA) that Included many Poor People

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) relates, "I was sitting with a group of Muhaajireen amongst whom were people who (because of poverty) had so little clothing that they were hiding behind each other. A Qaari of ours was busy reciting the Qur'aan and we were all busy listening to Allaah's Book. Rasulullaah ﷺ (arrived there and) said, 'All praise is for Allaah who has created in my Ummah people with whom I have been instructed to remain with.' The group turned and faced Rasulullaah ﷺ, who recognised none of them besides myself. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, 'O impoverished Muhaajireen, listen to the good news that you will have perfect light on the Day of Qiyaamah. You will enter Jannah half a day before the rich, which is equal to five hundred years.'" [^4]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Prefers the Gathering of Knowledge to the Gathering of Dhikr

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by two gatherings in his Masjid. While the people in one gathering were making du'aa to Allaah and concentrating on this, the other was learning and teaching Fiqh. Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "While both gatherings are doing excellent work, the one is superior than the other. As for the one, they are making du'aa to Allaah and concentrating on this. If Allaah wills, He shall grant them (what they ask) and if He wills, He may refuse them. As for the others, they are learning and teaching the ignorant and I have been sent as a teacher." Rasulullaah ﷺ
Abu Ya'la. Mundhiri (Vol.1 Pg.76) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Bayhaqi, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.57). Abu Nu'aym has reported the narration at greater length in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.342).
